prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, which opened the field of moire quantum materials.

statement.case_for: I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B038) with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. Round 1 did not weaken the core case: six of eight members prefer it with an identical three-name set, the two members who prefer B045 name it as their strongest alternative, and nobody disputes the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states or its reproduction by independent groups. The structure is a quantitative prediction (flat bands at a magic angle, 2011) that nature confirmed in 2018, followed by a field with one tunable control parameter. As a statistical physicist I value that the twist angle moves a system through a phase diagram in a controlled way, and the same control has since been carried to other moire platforms. The citation I propose rests on the prediction and on the observed states, and claims no pairing mechanism. My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1; what has changed is that I state my answer to the chair's mechanism question more explicitly (see responses).
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains maturity: the field is about eight years old, the superconducting mechanism is open, and twist-angle disorder makes quantitative comparison between devices harder than for a clock. Lindroth and Kroll press this fairly, and I do not dismiss it. The second reservation is credit: Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers, earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and other moire groups lie outside a three-name limit. I rely on recalled priority history here, not on a checked source, and I say so as the chair asks. I judge the Bistritzer-MacDonald paper to be the decisive prediction because it gave the magic angle and a quantitative flat-band condition, but that is a judgement about which contribution the citation should name, not a verified settlement of priority.

responses.point: Lindroth asks whether I would still support twisted bilayer graphene if the superconducting mechanism turned out to be conventional, whether the omission of her clock candidate is about merit or only novelty, and argues that seven years is short and the field is still being rewritten, whereas the clock has two decades of confirmation.
responses.response: Yes, my support would not change if the pairing turned out to be conventional. What I would award is the prediction of flat bands and the discovery that a gate-tunable flat band hosts correlated insulators and superconductivity at all; a conventional explanation would change the interpretation of one phase, not the existence of the platform. Fractional Chern states and the competing explanations you mention show a field that is expanding rather than being undone, and the citation avoids tying the prize to any one of them. On the clock, my ranking it only as an alternative is a judgement about novelty relative to 2005 and 2012 and about the discovery-versus-instrument criterion, not about merit: the science is excellent and the two-name credit is the cleanest on the list. I concede your point that maturity favours the clock and that twist-angle disorder makes cross-laboratory quantitative comparison weaker. I weigh breadth of new physics more heavily than completeness, and that is where we differ.

responses.point: Kroll says he would not oppose B038 if the committee converges there, but that its open questions are larger than those of clocks, and that the experimental first-author and group attribution cannot be resolved under the three-name cap. He also asks that a clock citation say what is specific to lattices versus ion clocks.
responses.response: I agree that the open questions are larger for B038, and I accept that the difference is one of weighting and not of science. Where I differ is that the open questions of B038 are about what the new phase diagram contains, which is a sign of a field rather than of an unfinished discovery. On attribution I do not claim the three names are free of dispute; I claim that the committee has to choose between a prize that names the decisive prediction and the decisive experimental group and a prize that tries to enumerate a community. Your point about ion versus lattice clocks is exactly the sort of specificity a B045 citation would need, and I would support it as my first alternative on that basis. I also note that your disclosed link to the Hall environment bears on B045, so I would not want the B045 case to depend on your weight alone.

responses.point: Olsson, who ranks B038 first, says the argument that it could be slightly early is the one she takes most seriously, and that device-to-device variation means some literature claims are sample-specific.
responses.response: I think we are close here. Her materials point is the one I rely on: independent groups learned to make devices good enough to see the same phase diagram, which is why I treat the discovery as settled even where individual claims are sample-specific. I would answer the early-versus-late question this way: waiting for the field to separate robust from sample-dependent physics has a cost, because the prediction-and-observation pairing is clearest now and the three names are unambiguous in the proposals. I would accept a citation phrased narrowly enough to cover only the robust content, the flat bands, the correlated insulators and the superconductivity, and to leave out claims that are still sample-specific.

responses.point: Eriksson ranked DMFT (B037) first in his opening and moved B038 to preferred, while still asking whether the field has produced a stable enough body of results for a prize.
responses.response: I welcome that he moved to B038 and treat the stability question as legitimate. The stable body of results is the existence of the flat-band-driven correlated and superconducting states and their reproduction across groups and platforms, and I would define the prize by that. I also note that his concern about Metzner outside the DMFT credit remains the main obstacle for B037, and I do not think it can be fixed within three names.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges eight years and an unsettled pairing mechanism enough reason to defer B038 for a mature, cleanly credited alternative such as B045.

Whether Yuan Cao and the earlier twisted-bilayer theorists can be adequately handled by wording alone within a three-name limit; several priority claims, including mine, rest on recollection and are not verified from a source.
Whether twist-angle disorder and sample-specific results are better described as technical or as signs that the robust physics is not yet fully separated.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile; none of the credited individuals for B038 or B045 is among my documented co-authors, supervisors or institutional colleagues, and my turbulence and neural-network work is unrelated. I note the disclosed flags of Kroll (B045), Johansson (B026, B007), Pearce (B016) and Eriksson (B037), none of which touches B038.
